chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Inform me — may I be your ransom — why did Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbid wine, carrion, blood, and swine flesh?'

He said: 'Allah, Glorified and Exalted, did not forbid those things to His servants and permit other things out of any desire for what He forbade them, nor out of any disinterest in what He permitted them. Rather, He created creation and the Mighty and Majestic knows what sustains their bodies and what benefits them, so He permitted it for them and authorised it as a grace from Him — Blessed and Exalted — for their welfare; and He knows what harms them, so He forbade them from it and prohibited it upon them.'

Then He made it permissible for the one in dire necessity and allowed it for him at the time when his body cannot survive without it, commanding him to take only what suffices as necessity, nothing more than that.

Then he said: As for carrion, no one habitually consumes it without his body weakening, his physique wasting away, his strength departing, and his lineage being cut off; and the eater of carrion does not die except suddenly.

And as for blood, it causes its consumer to develop jaundice, gives foul odour to the mouth, produces offensive breath, corrupts the character, breeds rabidity and hardness in the heart, and scarcity of compassion and mercy — to the point that one cannot be trusted not to kill his own child or parents, nor can he be trusted with his close companion or with whoever accompanies him.

And as for swine flesh, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, transformed a people into various forms resembling the pig, the ape, and the bear and whatever was among the mutants; then He forbade eating it as an exemplary warning, lest people benefit from it and belittle the severity of its punishment.

And as for wine, He prohibited it because of what it causes and its corrupting effects; and he said: The habitual wine-drinker is like a worshipper of idols. It causes him trembling, takes away his light, demolishes his moral dignity, and emboldens him to commit the forbidden — from shedding blood to committing adultery. When he is intoxicated, one cannot be assured that he will not assault his own family members while he has no awareness of it. And wine does not increase its drinker except in every evil.

key_terms.الدَّم: Blood (dam) — prohibited to consume; among the four categories explicitly forbidden in the Quran
key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (khamr) — any intoxicating beverage; its prohibition is among the most emphasised in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمَثُلَة: Exemplary punishment, cautionary sign — the swine prohibition is partly to preserve the gravity of divine punishment
key_terms.الْمَسْخ: Maskh — divine metamorphosis or transformation; a punishment in which people were changed into animal forms
key_terms.الْمَصْلَحَة: Welfare, benefit — the Imam uses this term to explain that divine permissions are aligned with human benefit
key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: Carrion (mayta) — the flesh of an animal that died without proper Islamic slaughter
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرّ: The one in dire necessity — Islamic law makes an exception for the desperate when facing death
key_terms.لَحْم الْخِنْزِير: Swine flesh — forbidden in the Quran; here explained via the concept of maskh (divine metamorphosis of a sinful people)

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah forbid wine, carrion, blood, and swine flesh according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains to his companion Mufaddal ibn Umar the rational and spiritual reasons behind four major Islamic prohibitions: wine, carrion, blood, and swine flesh. The Imam frames divine legislation not as arbitrary command but as divine wisdom aligned with human welfare — Allah permits what sustains the body and forbids what harms it. Each prohibition is given specific physiological and moral rationale, a remarkable example of the Imam's exposition of the hikmah (wisdom) behind the shari'ah, consistent with the Shia theological principle that divine rulings have inherent rational grounds (al-ta'lil).
